about: meetBlocks groups the join-irreducibles of [u ^ w, u v w] by COMPARABILITY,
and priceByBlocks prices each group. This is the localisation pair.
On a chain every irreducible is comparable to every other, so there is always
exactly ONE block: a case built only on a chain cannot tell a correct
partition from any other.
And every obvious valuation — index, index squared — is SUPERMODULAR, and
monotone with supermodular gives g = 0. A file built from those alone reports
zero premiums everywhere while looking thorough. `pricesAnything` exists to
say so: the runner calls it, and a case claiming a premium on a valuation
that prices nothing is refused.
Which lattices have anything to localise:
A BLOCK CONTRIBUTES A NON-ZERO PREMIUM ONLY IF THE SUBLATTICE IT GENERATES
CONTAINS AN INCOMPARABLE PAIR — for a MONOTONE INCREASING valuation, which
is the shape a design scale has, since worth rises with level. There
`priceByBlocks` returns 0 on all 81 pairs of a 9-rung chain, and the
spectrum collapses to {0}.
The condition is monotone, not every. A DECREASING valuation gives a non-zero
premium in 79 of those 81 pairs and a sawtooth one in 62. And `premium` and
`gap` are two quantities rather than one: on the same chain `gap` is 0 in
81/81 for an increasing valuation and non-zero in 64/81 for a decreasing one.
RI <= 0 does not license `g == 0` on its own. Monotone AND supermodular gives
zero counterexamples while either half alone leaves many, and among MONOTONE
valuations `g != 0` iff not supermodular, exactly. `pricesAnything` carries
both halves; `!isSupermodular` is IDENTICALLY FALSE on a chain, so a runner
that checks only that half passes vacuously.
B2 and M3 fall there for the plainest reason available: all their
join-irreducibles are atoms, so every pair meets at bottom, so every block is
a singleton, so every block generates the 2-chain {bottom, x}. Add a STEM —
one level between bottom and the atoms — and the atoms meet above bottom, the
block has something to price, and the localised total reconciles exactly.
That pair of cases is below, and it is what makes this a theorem rather than
a shrug.
A board that is a PRODUCT OF SCALES has its irreducibles only on the axes, so
two from different axes meet at bottom, so the blocks ARE the axes and each
axis is a chain. `priceByBlocks` is therefore identically zero on a product
of chains. B2 and M3 are not pathological corners; they are the smallest
members of that family.

coverage.criterion: a chain (one block, degenerate); B2 and M3 under a cheap join (blocks are singletons, so the localised total is zero while the whole prices 2); the SAME lattices with a stem, where the atoms meet above bottom and the total reconciles exactly; a product of two chains, which is the shape every real board has; and an interval holding no irreducible

cases.name: a chain has exactly one block, so it pins no partition
B2 under a cheap join: two incomparable atoms, two blocks
M3 under a cheap join: three incomparable atoms, three blocks
M3 from top to bottom takes in every irreducible and still splits three ways
B2 with a stem: the atoms meet ABOVE bottom, so the block prices and reconciles
a product of two chains: the blocks ARE the axes, and every axis is a chain
an interval holding no irreducible is empty, not one empty block
